title: What Is Talent? And Do You Need It to Learn English?
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: The potential or capacity to do something.
Related to genes or inherited traits.
The energy or work put into something.
To spend time or money to improve something.

sentences.en: “I’m just not good at learning languages.”
sentences.zh: “我就是不擅长学语言。”

sentences.en: I’m sure many of you listening right now have thought this before.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，现在听节目的很多人以前都这么想过。

sentences.en: And I’m sure you’ve thought the opposite about people you have met in the past: “Wow, she’s so talented at English” or “He has a gift for languages.”
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定，对于你过去遇到过的人，你也曾有过相反的想法：“哇，她的英语太有天赋了”或者“他很有语言天分。”

sentences.en: These kinds of comments are incredibly common.
sentences.zh: 这类评价非常普遍。

sentences.en: Many people believe that success in language learning depends mostly on talent.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为，学好语言主要取决于天赋。

sentences.en: Some people are just naturally good at learning English, while others aren’t.
sentences.zh: 有些人天生就擅长学英语，而另一些人则不然。

sentences.en: But is this true? Is talent real when it comes to learning languages?
sentences.zh: 但事实真的是这样吗？在语言学习这件事上，天赋真的存在吗？

sentences.en: And if talent does exist, what exactly is it?
sentences.zh: 如果天赋确实存在，它到底是什么呢？

sentences.en: Is it the same thing as skill?
sentences.zh: 它和技能是同一回事吗？

sentences.en: Is it the same thing as advantage? In today’s episode, we’re going to explore these questions.
sentences.zh: 它和优势是同一回事吗？在今天的节目中，我们将探讨这些问题。

sentences.en: We’ll look at what talent really means, how it is different from ability, advantage, and skill, and what science and neuroscience say about why some people seem to learn languages faster than others.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨天赋的真正含义，它与能力、优势和技能有何不同，以及科学和神经科学如何解释为什么有些人学语言似乎比其他人更快。

sentences.en: Then we’ll apply these ideas directly to English learning and hopefully give you all some motivation!
sentences.zh: 然后，我们将把这些理念直接应用到英语学习中，希望为大家注入一些动力！

sentences.en: Let’s start by clarifying the difference between ability and performance.
sentences.zh: 让我们首先厘清“能力（ability）”与“表现（performance）”的区别。

sentences.en: Ability refers to your potential to do something.
sentences.zh: 能力指的是你做某事的潜力。

sentences.en: It’s what you are capable of doing under the right conditions.
sentences.zh: 它是你在合适条件下能够做到的事情。

sentences.en: Performance is what you actually do in a real situation.
sentences.zh: 表现则是你在实际情况中所做出的实际行动。

sentences.en: So let’s imagine an example. Imagine you are going to run a marathon.
sentences.zh: 让我们设想一个例子。假设你要去跑马拉松。

sentences.en: You train really hard, and you now have the ability to run a marathon in under three hours.
sentences.zh: 你进行了刻苦的训练，现在你具备了在三小时内跑完马拉松的能力。

sentences.en: You have done this in training, so you know you have the ability.
sentences.zh: 你在训练中做到过这一点，所以你知道自己具备这种能力。

sentences.en: You can do it on a treadmill. You know you have the ability to run a marathon in under three hours.
sentences.zh: 你能在跑步机上做到。你知道自己有能力在三小时内跑完马拉松。

sentences.en: But when it comes to the actual marathon race, the weather is a little bit hot.
sentences.zh: 但到了真正的马拉松比赛时，天气有点热。

sentences.en: The course is full of hills, and there’s so many people around.
sentences.zh: 赛道上坡起伏不断，周围有那么多的人。

sentences.en: And you don’t finish in under three hours.
sentences.zh: 结果你没能在三小时内完赛。

sentences.en: You had the ability to do it, but your performance on the day was not the best.
sentences.zh: 你本来有这个能力，但你当天在赛场上的表现并不在最佳状态。

sentences.en: Performance is influenced by many different things.
sentences.zh: 表现会受到许多不同因素的影响。

sentences.en: My ability in Japanese is pretty good, but my performance can vary wildly.
sentences.zh: 我的日语能力相当不错，但我的表现却可能起伏不定。

sentences.en: If I’m stressed or nervous or tired or talking about a topic I’m not familiar with, my performance in speaking can drop significantly.
sentences.zh: 如果我感到压力、紧张、疲惫，或者在谈论一个我不熟悉的话题，我的口语表现就会显著下降。

sentences.en: This distinction, the difference between ability and performance, is important because we often judge people based on what we see.
sentences.zh: 这种区分——能力与表现的区别——非常重要，因为我们经常根据看到的情况来评判他人。

sentences.en: If someone performs well in front of you, you assume they have a high level of ability.
sentences.zh: 如果某人在你面前表现出色，你就会假设他们的能力水平很高。

sentences.en: Maybe they’re talented. If someone performs poorly, maybe you assume they have a lower ability.
sentences.zh: 也许他们很有天赋。如果某人表现不佳，你或许就会假设他们的能力较差。

sentences.en: They lack talent. I see this in my conversation clubs, the Thinking in English speaking practice groups that I run, you should all join.
sentences.zh: 他们缺乏天赋。我在我的交流俱乐部里经常看到这种情况——我运营的“Thinking in English”英语口语练习群，大家都应该来参加。

sentences.en: Some of my regular members have been attending for years.
sentences.zh: 我的一些老成员已经参加好几年了。

sentences.en: And depending on the topic or the time of day, their performance varies, but their ability is clearly strong and improving over time.
sentences.zh: 根据话题或一天的不同时间，他们的表现会有所起伏，但他们的能力明显很强，而且一直在不断进步。

sentences.en: But day to day, your performance can be different.
sentences.zh: 不过在日常生活中，你的表现可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: Okay. So when we’re talking about whether someone is a “good language learner” or a “talented student “, what we’re really thinking about, at least most of us, are thinking about “ability “.
sentences.zh: 好了。所以，当我们讨论某人是否是一个“优秀的语言学习者”或“有天赋的学生”时，我们真正想到的——至少对我们大多数人来说——其实是“能力”。

sentences.en: We’re thinking about what you are potentially able to do, your capability, your ability.
sentences.zh: 我们想到的是你潜在能做到的事情，你的潜能，你的能力。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, I was listening to a podcast that talked a little bit about being “good” at something and they made a really useful distinction between different parts of ability.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我听了一个播客节目，里面简短地谈到了在某事上“优秀”的概念，他们对能力的各个组成部分进行了非常实用的区分。

sentences.en: There’s talent, skill, and advantage. If you combine together these three things, you get your ability.
sentences.zh: 这里有天赋、技能和优势。如果你把这三者结合起来，就得到了你的能力。

sentences.en: At least a rough approximation of your ability.
sentences.zh: 至少这是对你能力的一个粗略估算。

sentences.en: So I think maybe we need to think a little bit in more detail about talent, skill, and advantage.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，我们或许需要更详细地思考一下天赋、技能和优势。

sentences.en: In my opinion, a good definition of “talent” is inborn potential or your natural ability.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，“天赋”的一个好定义是先天潜力或你的自然能力。

sentences.en: Some people seem to have brains that are slightly better suited to certain types of learning or thinking.
sentences.zh: 有些人似乎拥有更适合特定类型学习或思考的大脑。

sentences.en: For example, some people just have a better memory than other people.
sentences.zh: 例如，有些人的记忆力就是比其他人好。

sentences.en: Some people are great at pattern recognition.
sentences.zh: 有些人非常擅长模式识别。

sentences.en: These are both things that will make learning a language slightly easier.
sentences.zh: 这两点都会让学习一门语言变得稍微容易一些。

sentences.en: It won’t be a huge difference, but it will have an impact.
sentences.zh: 它不会造成巨大的差异，但确实会产生影响。

sentences.en: It’s obviously debatable whether someone’s ability is natural or learned, and most of the time it is a mix.
sentences.zh: 某人的能力究竟是天生的还是后天学来的，这显然存在争议，而且大多数时候两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: Think about an elite sprinter, like Usain Bolt.
sentences.zh: 想想顶级短跑运动员，比如尤塞恩·博尔特（Usain Bolt）。

sentences.en: Sprinters train incredibly hard, but they also seem to share some genetic similarities, like having a specific type of fiber in their muscles called “fast twitch fibers “.
sentences.zh: 短跑运动员训练极其刻苦，但他们似乎也具有某些共同的基因相似性，比如肌肉中有一种被称为“快肌纤维”的特定纤维。

sentences.en: And this genetic similarity gives them an innate talent for sprinting.
sentences.zh: 正是这种基因相似性赋予了他们短跑的先天天赋。

sentences.en: They have a natural talent for sprinting thanks to their bodies.
sentences.zh: 多亏了他们的身体，他们拥有短跑的天赋。

sentences.en: Another example of someone just being naturally talented is the American Football Player, the NFL player, Jordan Mailata.
sentences.zh: 另一个天生具有运动天赋的例子是美式橄榄球运动员、NFL球员乔丹·马拉塔（Jordan Mailata）。

sentences.en: If you are not an NFL fan, you probably don’t know who Jordan Mailata is.
sentences.zh: 如果你不是NFL球迷，你可能不知道乔丹·马拉塔是谁。

sentences.en: He plays for the Philadelphia Eagles. But he’s not from the USA.
sentences.zh: 他效力于费城老鹰队（Philadelphia Eagles）。但他不是美国人。

sentences.en: He grew up in Australia playing a completely different sport.
sentences.zh: 他在澳大利亚长大，玩的是一项完全不同的运动。

sentences.en: The sport of Rugby League. He got to a decently high level, but it became clear he was never going to become a professional.
sentences.zh: 也就是英式橄榄球（Ruggle League）。他达到了相当高的水平，但很明显他成不了职业选手。

sentences.en: He just wasn’t at the top level in the sport of Rugby League.
sentences.zh: 他只是在英式橄榄球这项运动中没有达到顶级水平。

sentences.en: He wasn’t going to become a professional.
sentences.zh: 他成不了职业选手。

sentences.en: So around the age of 20, he decided to try out for an NFL team.
sentences.zh: 所以在20岁左右的时候，他决定去试训NFL球队。

sentences.en: He had never played American football in his life, but he was naturally athletic.
sentences.zh: 他这辈子从来没玩过美式橄榄球，但他天生运动神经发达。

sentences.en: He was big, strong and quick. He was successful.
sentences.zh: 他身材高大、强壮且敏捷。他成功了。

sentences.en: He joined the Philadelphia Eagles, trained, became a regular player and is now considered one of the best in the entire league in his position.
sentences.zh: 他加入了费城老鹰队，经过训练成为了一名常规球员，现在被认为是联盟中该位置上最优秀的球员之一。

sentences.en: He didn’t grow up playing the sport. He didn’t practice NFL skills, American football skills for years and years and years.
sentences.zh: 他从小并没有这项运动的成长背景。他并没有练习美式橄榄球技能长达多年。

sentences.en: He was simply naturally gifted, naturally talented at being an athlete.
sentences.zh: 他只是作为一个运动员有着天然的赋能、天然的天赋。

sentences.en: Let’s go back to language learning. There are people out there who have this innate, inborn potential.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到语言学习。有些人确实拥有这种先天的潜力。

sentences.en: They have a naturally good memory, or they are naturally good at copying accents.
sentences.zh: 他们天生记忆力好，或者天生擅长模仿口音。

sentences.en: But, talent is just potential, right? You have to remember this.
sentences.zh: 但是，天赋仅仅是潜力，对吧？你必须记住这一点。

sentences.en: Talent does not mean you’re going to be skillful or successful.
sentences.zh: 天赋并不意味着你一定会变得熟练或成功。

sentences.en: Talent is just potential. I was watching the Winter Olympics recently.
sentences.zh: 天赋仅仅是潜力。我最近在看冬奥会。

sentences.en: And yes, everyone was an amazing athlete.
sentences.zh: 没错，每个人都是出色的运动员。

sentences.en: The skiers were amazing, the snowboarders were amazing.
sentences.zh: 滑雪运动员太棒了，单板滑雪运动员也太棒了。

sentences.en: But I couldn’t help think that there was someone out there in the world, living in a country with no ski slopes, that could be the most naturally talented skier or snowboarder in history.
sentences.zh: 但我禁不住想，世界上某个地方，生活在一个没有滑雪场的国家里，可能藏着历史上最有天赋的滑雪或单板滑雪天才。

sentences.en: They just haven’t had the chance. And this brings us to the next part of ability: “Advantage “.
sentences.zh: 他们只是没有得到机会。这就引出了能力的下一个组成部分：“优势（Advantage）”。

sentences.en: An advantage is a condition that gives someone a “head start” when learning or developing a skill.
sentences.zh: 优势是指在学习或培养某项技能时，能让人占得“先机”的条件。

sentences.en: It is a situation that makes learning something easier.
sentences.zh: 它是一种能让学习某事变得更容易的环境。

sentences.en: In my understanding, talent is based on your brain and genetics, while advantage comes from your environment.
sentences.zh: 据我理解，天赋基于你的大脑和基因，而优势则来自于你的环境。

sentences.en: Let’s go back to the Winter Olympics. I live in Japan, and a lot of the TV coverage here focused on the Japanese snowboarders who performed really well.
sentences.zh: 让我们回到冬奥会。我住在日本，这里很多电视报道都聚焦于表现出色的日本单板滑雪运动员。

sentences.en: They were clearly very athletic and talented, but watching their interviews, it also became clear they were very advantaged.
sentences.zh: 他们显然非常有运动天赋，但看着他们的采访，也很明显看出他们极具优势。

sentences.en: All of them came from the snowy and mountainous regions of Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们全都来自日本多雪和多山的地区。

sentences.en: That is an advantage. It’s really difficult to become a great skier, an Olympic level skier, if there’s no ski slopes for you to practice.
sentences.zh: 这就是优势。如果没有滑雪场让你练习，要成为一名伟大的滑雪运动员——奥运级别的滑雪运动员——是非常困难的。

sentences.en: And it’s really difficult to become a great snowboarder if there’s no ski slopes for you to practice.
sentences.zh: 而且如果没有滑雪场让你练习，要成为一名伟大的单板滑雪运动员也非常困难。

sentences.en: All of those snowboarders seemed to start skiing or snowboarding from a very early age, sometimes three or four or five years old.
sentences.zh: 所有这些单板滑雪运动员似乎在很小的时候就开始滑雪或单板滑雪了，有时只有三、四、五岁。

sentences.en: And they came from families in which their parents and their siblings also skied and snowboarded.
sentences.zh: 而且他们出身于父母和兄弟姐妹也滑雪和玩单板滑雪的家庭。

sentences.en: That’s another advantage, coming from a family that takes you skiing early.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种优势，生在一个带你早早去滑雪的家庭里。

sentences.en: Winter sports are also not cheap. It requires ski passes and lessons and equipment.
sentences.zh: 冬季运动也不便宜。它需要滑雪通行证、课程和装备。

sentences.en: You need money to go skiing, and you need money to ski regularly, and you need to ski regularly to become an Olympic athlete.
sentences.zh: 你需要钱去滑雪，你需要钱定期滑雪，而且你需要定期滑雪才能成为一名奥运选手。

sentences.en: I’m not saying that the Winter Olympians didn’t work hard to become great athletes.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说冬奥选手没有通过努力工作来成为伟大的运动员。

sentences.en: Yes, they did. They worked really hard. And I’m sure many of them are naturally talented as well, but they are almost all advantaged as well.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们付出了。他们非常努力。而且我确信他们中的许多人也很有天赋，但他们几乎也都占据了优势。

sentences.en: Their advantages help them become an Olympian.
sentences.zh: 他们的优势帮助他们成为了奥运选手。

sentences.en: The fact they live near a mountain or the fact that their father snowboarded and took them snowboarding every weekend.
sentences.zh: 他们住在山附近这一事实，或者他们的父亲玩单板滑雪并在每个周末带他们去滑雪这一事实。

sentences.en: So what are advantages when it comes to language learning?
sentences.zh: 那么，在语言学习方面，优势是什么呢？

sentences.en: For example, imagine someone who grew up in a bilingual household.
sentences.zh: 例如，想象一个在双语家庭中长大的人。

sentences.en: From childhood they regularly heard two languages spoken at home, which helps to develop your listening skills and gets people used to switching between languages.
sentences.zh: 从童年起，他们经常在家里听到两种语言交替使用，这有助于培养你的听力技能，并让人习惯于在不同语言之间切换。

sentences.en: This doesn’t necessarily need to be English and your native language.
sentences.zh: 这不一定非得是英语和你的母语。

sentences.en: There is some evidence that it is easier for bilingual people to learn a third language as well.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，双语人群学习第三门语言也会更容易一些。

sentences.en: Because they already have the skills, and the knowledge, and they’re used to learning languages in this way.
sentences.zh: 因为他们已经具备了技能和知识，并且习惯了用这种方式学习语言。

sentences.en: So if you have talent and you have advantage, are you going to be great at something?
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你既有天赋又有优势，你就会在某事上变得非常优秀吗？

sentences.en: No. Perhaps the most important part of ability is “skill “.
sentences.zh: 不。能力中或许最重要的一部分是“技能（Skill）”。

sentences.en: Skill is the result of training, practice and repetition.
sentences.zh: 技能是训练、练习和重复的结果。

sentences.en: Skill is something you develop over time through your effort and experience.
sentences.zh: 技能是你通过努力和经验随着时间推移而培养出来的东西。

sentences.en: Talent is something in your body. Advantage is something in your environment.
sentences.zh: 天赋是存在于你身体里的东西。优势是存在于你环境中的东西。

sentences.en: Skill is something you build. We’re talking about language learning, so most of the things that we admire in a fluent speaker, you guys admire in a fluent speaker of English or I admire in a fluent Japanese speaker, are skills.
sentences.zh: 技能是你亲手构建的东西。我们正在讨论语言学习，所以我们在一个流利说话者身上钦佩的大多数东西——你们在流利的英语说话者身上钦佩的，或者我在流利的日语说话者身上钦佩的——都是技能。

sentences.en: Clear pronunciation is a skill that most people improve through listening and practicing sounds.
sentences.zh: 清晰的发音是一种技能，大多数人通过聆听和练习发音来提升它。

sentences.en: The ability to write clearly and logically in English develops through reading and writing and getting lots of feedback.
sentences.zh: 用英语清晰且合乎逻辑地写作的能力是通过阅读、写作以及获得大量反馈培养出来的。

sentences.en: Using advanced vocabulary normally comes from repeated exposure to words in context.
sentences.zh: 使用高级词汇通常来自于在语境中对单词的反复接触。

sentences.en: And speaking fluently is usually the result of many, many hours of conversation and practice.
sentences.zh: 而流利地说话通常是成百上千小时对话和练习的结果。

sentences.en: You can become highly skilled even if you are not naturally talented.
sentences.zh: 即使你没有与生俱来的天赋，你也能变得技艺精湛。

sentences.en: If you work hard and you practice consistently for years… yes, you can become a high level speaker.
sentences.zh: 如果你努力工作并坚持不懈地练习多年……是的，你可以成为一名高水平的说话者。

sentences.en: Let’s think of a few more examples showing the difference between talent, advantage, and skill.
sentences.zh: 让我们再想几个例子来展示天赋、优势和技能之间的区别。

sentences.en: Some English learners seem to have a naturally good accent.
sentences.zh: 有些英语学习者似乎天生就拥有很好的口音。

sentences.en: They can copy sounds easily and speak in a way that feels quite similar to me, perhaps.
sentences.zh: 他们能轻松地模仿发音，并且用一种对我来说可能感觉相当相似的方式说话。

sentences.en: This might come from talent. For example, they might have a strong phonetic memory.
sentences.zh: 这可能来自于天赋。例如，他们可能拥有很强的语音记忆。

sentences.en: Phonetic memory is a memory for sounds. And it can let someone hear small differences in sounds and then make them accurately.
sentences.zh: 语音记忆是对声音的记忆。它能让人听到声音的微小差异，然后准确地模仿出来。

sentences.en: I do not have a strong phonetic memory, right?
sentences.zh: 我可没有很强的语音记忆，对吧？

sentences.en: I’m terrible at reproducing sounds. There can also be advantage.
sentences.zh: 我复刻声音的能力太差了。这里面也可能存在优势。

sentences.en: Maybe people grew up watching English TV or had a foreign teacher as a young child.
sentences.zh: 也许这些人从小看着英语电视长大，或者在幼年时有一位外教。

sentences.en: But of course there’s a lot of skill required.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这也需要大量的技能。

sentences.en: Most of the time, clear pronunciation comes from practice.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，清晰的发音来自于练习。

sentences.en: A lot of practice. You need to spend a lot of time repeating sounds, shadowing audio, understanding common mistakes.
sentences.zh: 大量的练习。你需要花大量时间重复发音、进行影子跟读、理解常见错误。

sentences.en: Another example is with vocabulary. Some people seem to remember new words instantly.
sentences.zh: 另一个例子是关于词汇的。有些人似乎能瞬间记住新单词。

sentences.en: This could be a form of talent, like having strong memory systems.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种天赋的形式，比如拥有强大的记忆系统。

sentences.en: Advantage matters too. Someone who grew up reading a lot, even if it’s in your native language, people who grew up reading tend to have better vocabulary learning ability than someone who’d never read as a child.
sentences.zh: 优势同样重要。一个从小大量阅读的人——哪怕是用你的母语，从小阅读的人往往比小时候从不阅读的人拥有更好的词汇学习能力。

sentences.en: And then most importantly, vocabulary is a skill.
sentences.zh: 然后最重要的是，词汇是一种技能。

sentences.en: It takes practice. So I want to end this episode with some advice.
sentences.zh: 它需要练习。所以我想以一些建议来结束这期节目。

sentences.en: First, give yourself advantages to help improve your ability.
sentences.zh: 首先，为自己创造优势以帮助提升你的能力。

sentences.en: You are all adults now, or most of you listening are adults now, but you can still give yourself advantages.
sentences.zh: 你们现在都是成年人了，或者听节目的多数人都是成年人了，但你们仍然可以为自己争取优势。

sentences.en: Maybe you live far away from any English speaking communities, but you can still surround yourself with English.
sentences.zh: 也许你住得离任何英语交流社区都很远，但你仍然可以用英语包围自己。

sentences.en: Podcasts or videos. My conversation and speaking groups, the Conversation Club on Patreon.
sentences.zh: 播客或视频。我的交流和口语小组，Patreon上的对话俱乐部。

sentences.en: Using social media. If you force yourself to be in an English environment, you have an advantage.
sentences.zh: 使用社交媒体。如果你强迫自己处于一个英语环境中，你就拥有了优势。

sentences.en: You can invest in classes or invest in textbooks.
sentences.zh: 你可以投资课程或投资教科书。

sentences.en: Give yourself every opportunity, every advantage, to improve.
sentences.zh: 给自己每一个机会、每一个优势来获得提升。

sentences.en: If you are lucky enough to have a natural strength, some kind of talent, try to build on it.
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运，拥有某种天然的优势或某种天赋，试着在此基础上进行构建。

sentences.en: For example, if you have a good memory, use your memory to help you study.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你记忆力很好，利用你的记忆力来帮助你学习。

sentences.en: But I’m sure many of you assume you are not talented language learners.
sentences.zh: 但我确信你们很多人都认为自己不是有语言天赋的学习者。

sentences.en: I think I am not a naturally talented language learner.
sentences.zh: 我认为自己也不是一个天生有语言天赋的学习者。

sentences.en: Perhaps you think you are bad at English.
sentences.zh: 也许你觉得自己英语不好。

sentences.en: Most of the time though, people just haven’t tried the right study methods or given themselves enough time or shown enough consistency.
sentences.zh: 不过大多数时候，人们只是没有尝试正确的学习方法，或者没有给自己足够的时间，或者没有表现出足够的持续性。

sentences.en: Overall, skill is the most important factor.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，技能才是最重要的因素。

sentences.en: Talent and advantage can help you, but if you study hard and you work hard, you will learn.
sentences.zh: 天赋和优势可以帮助你，但如果你刻苦学习、努力工作，你就会学会。

sentences.en: Repeat. Practice. Be consistent. Expose yourself to English.
sentences.zh: 重复。练习。保持持续性。让自己接触英语。

sentences.en: Have a great teacher. Join some classes.
sentences.zh: 找一个好老师。加入一些课程。

sentences.en: Join my conversation club. Listen to podcasts.
sentences.zh: 加入我的对话俱乐部。听播客。

sentences.en: Read books. Practice, practice, practice.
sentences.zh: 读书。练习，练习，再练习。

sentences.en: And you can become a high level English speaker.
sentences.zh: 你就能成为一名高水平的英语说话者。

sentences.en: What is talent? Well, in my view, talent is one of the components of ability.
sentences.zh: 什么是天赋？好吧，在我看来，天赋是能力的组成部分之一。

sentences.en: It is your natural, innate qualities that give you a head start.
sentences.zh: 它是你天生具备的、能让你占得先机的特质。

sentences.en: When you combine talent with advantage and especially skill, it makes up your overall ability.
sentences.zh: 当你把天赋与优势、尤其是技能结合起来时，它就构成了你的整体能力。

sentences.en: The reality is that most of the people you think are “talented language learners” are not necessarily talented in my definition.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，你认为的那些“有语言天赋的学习者”大多数并不一定符合我所定义的有天赋。

sentences.en: It’s more likely that they were “advantaged,” given opportunities and motivation to learn languages while young, and that they have built their skills through years of hard work.
sentences.zh: 更有可能的情况是，他们占了“优势”，在年轻时获得了学习语言的机会和动力，并且通过多年的刻苦努力建立了自己的技能。

sentences.en: If you want to improve your English ability, perhaps think about the following questions: What are you naturally talented at and how can you use this to learn?
sentences.zh: 如果你想提高你的英语能力，或许可以思考以下问题：你有什么天然的天赋，以及如何利用它来学习？

sentences.en: What advantages can you give yourself? And how are you working to develop your skills?
sentences.zh: 你能为自己创造哪些优势？你又是如何努力培养自己的技能的？
